found_by: the in-process fuzzer, read-only mode, 137 inputs into a campaign seeded from s03
base: mke2fs -t ext4 -b 1024 -g 1024 -N 128 -I 256 -O metadata_csum,64bit,extent,dir_index,^resize_inode -J size=1 on 4 MiB, one file /d/a
note_on_base: Rebuilt smaller than the artifact the fuzzer produced. The original was a 6 MiB s03 mutant carrying 300 KiB of incompressible random data, which does not gzip; this reproduces the same two edits on a volume that compresses to six kilobytes. The bug is a property of the superblock, not of the file data.

edits.what: superblock s_checksum (offset 0x3FC), re-stamped so the volume still passes the checksum gate

symptom: ext4b_probe accepted an inode size larger than the block size, and ext4_fs_inode_checksum then read s_inode_size bytes out of a block-sized buffer on the first readdir: AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow at ext4_fs.c:739, reached from __ext4_fs_get_inode_ref via ext4b_readdir. Six bytes on the medium, an out-of-bounds read from an `ls`.
why_it_was_reachable: Only because the mutator re-stamped the superblock checksum. Without that the volume is refused at the gate and nothing downstream runs -- which is the argument for having a stamper, demonstrated rather than asserted.
